name: trade_arrival_rate_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Trade arrival rate (number of trades per unit time) follows a predictable intraday pattern (U-shaped: high at open/close, low at midday). When the actual arrival rate deviates significantly from the expected pattern, it signals unusual activity — likely informed trading or news-driven flow. A sudden spike in trade arrival rate (>2x expected) with consistent price direction signals momentum that will persist for 3-8 minutes. Conversely, a spike with no net price change signals churn and imminent reversal. The inefficiency persists because: (1) trade count data is not displayed on most Indian retail platforms, (2) computing expected intraday arrival profiles requires historical calibration, and (3) the signal fires infrequently (2-4 times/day), making it unattractive for high-frequency strategies.
mechanism: Order flow imbalance between aggressive buyers and sellers creates short-term price pressure. When buy-side aggression exceeds sell-side by a threshold, the order book tilts and market makers adjust their quotes upward. This creates a 15-45 second drift before the book rebalances as new limit orders arrive to capture the improved price.

indicators.name: trade_count
indicators.formula: number of trades in each 1-min bar

indicators.name: expected_trade_count
indicators.formula: SMA of trade_count at same time-of-day over last 20 sessions

indicators.name: arrival_direction
indicators.formula: sign(close - open) of the anomaly bar

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter (anomaly detection is self-calibrating)
filters.volume_filter: volume_1min must also be > 1.5x expected (confirms trade count anomaly)

weaknesses: Low trade frequency (2-4/day) means long periods of inactivity and high variance in daily P&L. May have weeks of flat or negative returns.
Expected trade count profile requires 20+ days of calibration data; newly listed or recently volatile stocks will have stale profiles.
Cannot distinguish news-driven spikes (which may persist all day) from algorithmic order bursts (which revert quickly). Wrong classification leads to wrong hold time.
prior_art: Engle & Russell (1998) 'Autoregressive Conditional Duration' — foundational work on trade arrival modeling. Hawkes (1971) point process models applied to trade arrivals by Bacry et al. (2015). In Indian context, Mukherjee & Mishra (2010) study NSE microstructure.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
